questionText:
Read the following technical case analysis on cinematography and camera stabilization and answer the questions that follow:

In 1975, American cameraman Garrett Brown revolutionized visual grammar by inventing the 'Steadicam'. Prior to this breakthrough, cinematographers faced an intractable binary choice: either mount the camera on heavy, rigid metal tracks and wheeled dollies (silky-smooth but constrained by flat terrain and costly track-laying) or operate the camera handheld (nimble and portable but marred by erratic body shakes and tremors). Brown engineered a mechanical stabilization rig combining an articulated, spring-loaded iso-elastic arm, a lightweight vest distributing weight across the operator's torso, and a counterbalanced gimbal sled with a monitor. The Steadicam isolated the camera from the operator's physical footsteps and jolts. Stanley Kubrick famously harnessed the technology in 'The Shining' (1980), hiring Garrett Brown to navigate a Steadicam in 'Low Mode' just inches off the floor, gliding menacingly behind young Danny Torrance pedaling his tricycle through the labyrinthine carpeted hallways of the Overlook Hotel, creating an unprecedented visual sensation of ghostly, predatory tracking.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

Garrett Brown

Garrett Brown invented the Steadicam in 1975, transforming camera movement in cinema history.

questionText: In Indian jurisprudence, what is the fundamental difference between Civil Defamation and Criminal Defamation?

options.text: Civil defamation is tried exclusively by municipal police; Criminal defamation is tried by doctors
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Civil defamation is punished by hanging; Criminal defamation requires a five-rupee fine
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Civil defamation applies only to books; Criminal defamation applies only to radio
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: Civil defamation is an uncodified tort adjudicated in civil courts seeking monetary damages; Criminal defamation is codified under Sections 499 & 500 IPC punishing offenders with up to 2 years imprisonment
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Civil vs Criminal Defamation.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Communication Concepts and Theories (Civil vs Criminal Defamation):
Civil defamation is an uncodified tort adjudicated in civil courts seeking monetary damages; Criminal defamation is codified under Sections 499 & 500 IPC punishing offenders with up to 2 years imprisonment

Detailed Analysis:
Civil defamation seeks financial compensation for loss of reputation under tort law; criminal defamation under IPC 499/500 imposes fine and/or imprisonment.
Hence, Option C is correct.

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.
